verdict.rationale: Smithery's maintained CLI gives agents on-demand tool discovery and invocation (`smithery tool find [query]`, `tool get`, `tool call`) instead of preloading every definition. That is runtime search-and-load, but the evidence never describes it as in-context meta-tools or quantifies any context savings. Hosted 'Connect, and Toolbox' services shut down on 2026-10-31, so it is unclear whether connection-based tool calls still work. Missing for 10: documented meta-tools exposed to the agent (e.g. an MCP search/load tool), evidence of context-reduction behavior, clear post-shutdown status of connection-based tool loading, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can search and load tools at runtime through meta-tools instead of having thousands of tool definitions stuffed into my context

citations.quote: smithery tool list [connection], smithery tool find [query], smithery tool get <connection> <tool>, smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]
Smithery CLI connects your agents to thousands of skills and MCP servers directly from the command line.
